svg.title: A client who has HIV and reports consistent antiretroviral adherence returns for follow-up labs. Test Result Normal range CD4 count 180 cells/mm3 (down from prior visit) 500–1,200 cells/mm3 CD4:CD8 ratio 0.6 2:1 HIV viral load Rising over the past 3 months None detected (goal of treatment)
svg.desc: A CD4:CD8 ratio under 1 signals severe disease, and a falling CD4 count with a rising viral load despite reported adherence suggests the current regimen is failing, most likely from drug resistance. The provider needs to be notified so resistance testing can guide a regimen change; the client should never simply stop antiretroviral therapy, since that removes viral suppression entirely and worsens outcomes. Dismissing the trend as normal fluctuation is incorrect because a ratio of 0.6 with a rising viral load on therapy is a concerning, not benign, pattern.
